Retained premise: Gaussian tolerance premise: optimum temperature -> peak survivability -> decline with deviation. Learned use: preserve the typed sequence and its consumer; transfer boundary: Specify whether the distribution describes preference, presence, survival, or movement probability.

Retained premise: peak-and-tail consequence: temperature deviation -> lower suitability -> migration pressure. Learned use: preserve the typed sequence and its consumer; transfer boundary: Do not treat a probability density as population abundance without calibration.

Retained premise: bounded-growth premise: stable environment -> logistic growth -> saturation. Learned use: preserve the typed sequence and its consumer; transfer boundary: Fishing mortality and environmental variation must be addressed or declared absent.

Retained premise: capacity interpretation: grid environment -> finite K -> population ceiling. Learned use: preserve the typed sequence and its consumer; transfer boundary: Define the population unit represented by K.

Retained premise: extreme-event exclusion: no volcanic shock -> no abrupt SST jump -> retained warming trend. Learned use: preserve the typed sequence and its consumer; transfer boundary: This is a scenario boundary, not evidence that extremes cannot occur.

Retained premise: assumption-to-model consequence close: four premises -> linear forecast and CA rules -> sensitivity obligations. Learned use: preserve the typed sequence and its consumer; transfer boundary: Each simplification should have a violation test before recommendation.

contributions.summary: Places frequency inspection and moving-average treatment before coefficient estimation, making preprocessing part of the declared model interface.
Connects prediction error, mean-square minimization, autocorrelation, a Toeplitz system, and Levinson-Durbin recursion rather than presenting a coefficient vector without derivation.
Uses 2012 species overlays to create species-specific temperature intervals consumed by future location maps.
Converts thermal preference differences across a Moore neighborhood into an explicit directional movement interface.
Separates herring and mackerel logistic rates and then modifies capacity by local thermal conditions.
Turns annual CA states into best, worst, modal, and modal-frequency timing outputs intended for company decisions.
Defines five factors and five rating labels, then keeps each of three strategies in a parallel matrix-to-membership calculation.
Revises weights and matrices under a jurisdiction assumption instead of repeating the baseline ranking unchanged.
Reports a full five-by-five perturbation table, which is reusable as a local module check when not overstated as whole-pipeline validation.
Reorders technical evidence into a compact historical table, four location maps, a timing table, and plain-language actions for industry readers.

independent_extensions.summary: scenario-ensemble SST extension: replace one autoregressive extrapolation with climate-model scenarios, calibrated uncertainty, and spatial holdout comparison.
multi-driver habitat extension: combine temperature with currents, food, predators, depth, spawning constraints, and species observations through ablation-tested habitat suitability.
mass-conserving CA extension: specify synchronous movement, binomial transfers, recruitment, fishing mortality, seeds, and replicate convergence tests.
geodesic-access extension: replace one-grid distance with port coordinates, vessel range, anisotropic cell geometry, weather, fuel, and trip duration.
auditable MCDA extension: elicit weights and memberships from named stakeholders, test consistency, propagate uncertainty, and report Pareto tradeoffs alongside fuzzy ratings.
legal-economic scenario extension: overlay authoritative territorial/EEZ boundaries and quotas, then estimate capital, operating, processing, market, and transition costs.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Five compact visual blocks expose the complete physical-to-decision route and headline quantities before technical detail.
A forward route preview makes every later forecast, simulation, decision, scenario, and audience deliverable easy to locate.
The formula derivation is followed immediately by pseudocode and an error table, which improves traceability even though holdout status remains unresolved.
Six comparable maps make the claimed northward movement rapidly scannable and connect directly to the later access model.
A flowchart and a compact case table place mechanism and decision timing adjacent to one another.
Parallel option subsections make the three matrix calculations comparable, although the prose label reversal harms reliability.
A numeric perturbation table followed by explicit strengths and weaknesses signals an effort to bound the model's use.
The article changes vocabulary and ordering for a fishery audience while retaining source tables, maps, timing, and strategy choices.

models.summary: moving-average low-pass filter: Smooth annual SST before or after forecasting as implemented. Interface x, n, omega -> y; 1 numbered equations retained; status partial; handoff and limitations remain explicit.

autoregressive linear predictor: Represent an SST sample by p lagged annual values. Interface x, n, p, omega_p -> x_hat, e, a_p; 5 numbered equations retained; status partial; handoff and limitations remain explicit.

Yule-Walker normal equations: Estimate predictor coefficients from finite autocorrelation. Interface x, p, N -> a_p, r_x; 8 numbered equations retained; status partial; handoff and limitations remain explicit.
Levinson-Durbin recursion: Solve the Toeplitz predictor system. Interface r_x -> a_p; 1 numbered equations retained; status partial; handoff and limitations remain explicit.

Moore-neighborhood cellular automaton: Update fish population state on a regional grid. Interface s_ij, i, j, t -> f; 1 numbered equations retained; status partial; handoff and limitations remain explicit.
Gaussian thermal tolerance: Convert a half-degree tolerance into a normal spread. Interface X, mu -> P, sigma; 2 numbered equations retained; status partial; handoff and limitations remain explicit.

thermal-gradient migration probability: Move fish toward neighboring water with higher thermal preference. Interface T0, T1, T2, sigma, phi -> P_M; 1 numbered equations retained; status partial; handoff and limitations remain explicit.

logistic reproduction: Advance fish population toward carrying capacity. Interface K_cap, alpha, r_rate, t -> N_pop; 1 numbered equations retained; status partial; handoff and limitations remain explicit.
herring logistic calibration: Parameterize herring reproduction. Interface t -> N_pop; 1 numbered equations retained; status partial; handoff and limitations remain explicit.
mackerel logistic calibration: Parameterize mackerel reproduction. Interface t -> N_pop; 1 numbered equations retained; status partial; handoff and limitations remain explicit.

temperature-dependent carrying capacity: Reduce local capacity away from thermal optimum. Interface K_T0, f_T0, f_T1, T0, T1 -> K_T1; 1 numbered equations retained; status partial; handoff and limitations remain explicit.

task_reconstruction.decision: Choose company adaptation under baseline access loss and a foreign-water scenario while preserving uncertainty, legal, and feasibility boundaries.
inputs: Gaussian migration and logistic reproduction premises
task_reconstruction.objective: Forecast 2020-2069 Scottish-region SST and likely herring/mackerel locations, estimate access-loss timing for small fishing companies, compare adaptations, and communicate results to an industry audience.

unresolved_questions.summary: No separate official 2020 Problem A statement was found; the paper's five-question restatement is the available task source.
The exact Hadley product version, download date, missing-value handling, spatial bounds, and annual aggregation recipe are not fully reported.
The effective sample size, conditioning, regularization, fitted coefficient vector, and true train/test split remain unresolved.
The sample size, marker provenance, uncertainty, season, depth, and validation of the inferred temperature intervals are not stated.
The exact coordinate-to-cell mapping and the kilometer interpretation of a one-degree cell are incomplete.
The biological meaning of N=10000, carrying capacity, species growth rates, mortality, and fishing pressure is not calibrated.
Seeds, the complete 1000-run controller, stopping logic, full distributions, and convergence diagnostics are absent from the printed appendix.
Asset values, relocation distances, vessel costs, revenue, implementation time, and exchange-rate assumptions are not quantified.
No respondent set, elicitation protocol, consistency analysis, or uncertainty distribution is supplied for weights and matrices.
The map extent is not reconciled with authoritative territorial waters, EEZ boundaries, quotas, or access agreements.
Processing capacity, raw-fish supply, products, demand, regulation, capital cost, operating cost, and net value are not modeled.
The coefficient perturbation is not propagated through temperature fields, species locations, access timing, or strategy memberships.
The magazine's causal opening and benefits of relocation/processing need the same evidence qualifications as the technical body.
Printed code dimensions, year vectors, stochastic terms, rejection rules, missing conditional syntax, and output arrays do not yet form an executable parity package.
Initialization provenance, simultaneous-update semantics, migration conservation, function calls, outer repeats, and result export remain incomplete.

weaknesses.summary: Section 6.2 computes all-assets as good, some-assets as excellent, and vessels as average, but Section 6.3 reverses the first two labels while recommending partial relocation.
The printed SST code contains 'sum(isnan(series))' without a visible conditional keyword, so the displayed program is not syntactically reproducible as printed.
The SST output declares a 100-step time dimension while the printed assignment supplies only 1970:2019, leaving the historical-plus-forecast calendar inconsistent.
The order-50 predictor appears to be estimated from only 50 annual observations, leaving no clear residual degrees of freedom and making the Toeplitz system vulnerable to ill-conditioning.
The 2016-2019 inspection may reuse years included in coefficient estimation, so Table 4 is not proven to be an out-of-sample backtest.
Forecast noise is sampled only as a positive addition and threshold rejection selectively redraws paths, which can manufacture an upward trend beyond the fitted predictor.
Equation 17 prints 99.37 percent for a three-sigma interval; the standard normal mass within plus or minus three sigma is approximately 99.73 percent.
Equation 23 describes a ratio of normal-density values, while the appendix new_num implementation uses normcdf ratios, so equation and code do not implement the same capacity rule.
move_num receives a scalar population, so length(pos_curr) equals one and the loop can move at most one unit to each neighbor rather than sampling from the whole population.
next_state adds migrants to destinations but overwrites the source using reproduction from the original population, so outgoing migration is not visibly conserved.
The appendix does not visibly implement the claimed 1000-run outer experiment or its first-inaccessible-year stopping rule, preventing code-to-Table-6 parity.
The paper treats a one-degree grid as roughly 70-100 km, although longitude width varies with latitude and differs from latitude width; the access boundary is anisotropic.
The fuzzy weight vector and judgment matrices have no documented elicitation sample, consistency procedure, measurement scale, or uncertainty analysis.
Figure 12 treats disappearance beyond the plotted map extent as movement into another country's territorial waters, but map extent is not a legal maritime boundary.
The sensitivity analysis perturbs only linear-predictor coefficients and does not propagate uncertainty through species matching, CA timing, or fuzzy strategy ranking.
